title: Reindex and simplify tenant->deployment join path to reduce control-plane query tail latencies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
The control plane has a long tail on several user-facing endpoints that join tenant -> deployments -> routes. Investigation shows multiple overlapping indexes, nullable columns in join predicates, and ORM patterns that force sequential scans for low-cardinality tenants. These queries are contributing to sporadic 95th/99th percentile latency spikes and increased CPU billing in production.

Scope of work:
- Audit slow queries via pg_stat_statements and add representative EXPLAIN ANALYZE traces for top 6 slow query patterns.
- Consolidate and recreate indexes: drop redundant single-column indexes left from older migrations and build two focused indexes: one composite index covering (tenant_id, deployment_id, status) and a partial index for active deployments (status = 'active') to reduce bloat.
- Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and follow low-lock patterns for production migrations.
- Rewrite 3 ORM queries (DeploymentRepository.findByTenantWithLatestRoute, RouteService.listForTenant, and RolloutController.activeDeployments) to take advantage of the new index path and avoid JOINs where unnecessary by using indexed subqueries.
- Add background backfill for legacy nullable fields (coalesce to non-null) to ensure index selectivity is reliable.
- Add automated benchmarks (tpch-like synthetic workload + real-sampled request replays) and tie results into the perf dashboard.
- Update runbook and roll out as a canary: deploy migration to staging, then to a small-config production shard during off-peak, monitor error/latency dashboards, and proceed to full rollout with the ability to roll back by re-creating dropped indexes if necessary.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- All SQL migrations must be written as idempotent scripts with explicit rollback steps and instruction for manual intervention when CONCURRENTLY fails (index build is interrupted).
- Avoid long table locks; any schema changes that require locks must be deferred or coordinated with ops and scheduled in the maintenance window.
- Testing steps include local explain plans with pg_stat_statements enabled, production-like dataset runs in the perf cluster, and load testing with replayed traces.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th and 99th percentile latency for the affected endpoints reduce by at least 40% in staging perf runs and show consistent improvement in production canary.
- No increase in deadlocks or timeouts during migration window.
- Migration scripts and PRs approved with +2 reviews and perf benchmark attached.

2025-11-10 - Design review: Decided to prefer a partial index for active deployments to keep index size small. Also agreed to backfill null statuses to 'inactive' to avoid index selectivity surprises.
